hero.title: DENTISTRY IN FRANCE FOR FOREIGN STUDENTS

sections.title: 1. In France the study of dentistry takes five years.

items: The normal route to the ** French state dental qualification ** is typically ** six years ** . The amount of time spent in **specialist training** can vary and depends on the specialty you choose and the training route.

sections.title: 2. Can Indian students pursue dentistry in France after Class 12?

items: Yes, **Indian students can look for applications to French higher education** but they need to fulfill the **academic, language, admission and visa criteria. They must follow the correct **Campus France procedure** and understand that admission to dentistry is competitive.

sections.title: 3. Do I need NEET to study dentistry in France?

items: Dental studies have their own admission rules in French universities. NEET is an Indian examination. However, Indian students should check current **Indian regulatory requirements** before choosing a foreign dental program, especially if they intend to return to India to practise.

sections.title: 4. Is Dentistry taught in English in France?

items: The majority of **undergraduate dental programs in France** are taught mainly in **French**, including clinical training. Students wishing to undertake an English language programme are advised to check the language of delivery with the institution and not to assume that the programme will be taught entirely in English.

sections.title: 5. How much does dentistry tuition cost in France?

items: Costs vary by university, student fee category and living arrangements. *Standard public-university registration fees* are relatively low, but *differentiated fees* may be charged to some non-EU students. The budget must also include **costs for living expenses, accommodation, insurance** and other costs.

sections.title: 8. **How Does Accreditation and Recognition Work for Dentistry in France?**

items: Students must follow the required curriculum and sit the necessary exams to be eligible to gain the qualification.

However, graduating from a dental program and being **licensed to practice** are two different things. **Professional registration** and other requirements must be fulfilled before a person can practice as a dentist.
****Recognition in other countries****
If you plan to return to India or practice in another country, you should check the rules of the relevant **dental regulator** **before you enrol**.
Recognition may depend on the country, the institution, the qualification, the structure of clinical training and any licensing examinations or registration procedures required.

Graduates who have achieved the necessary qualifications and fulfilled the relevant **professional registration requirements** can seek ****dental careers in France**** and overseas, subject to the local regulations.
Opportunities
**Possible career paths:**
- General dentists.
- **Dentist in a dental office or medical office**.
- **Dental specialist** following recognized additional training .
- **Dental academic or research professional**.
- **Oral health educator or public health professional** if suitably qualified.
- **Dental sector jobs** in research, education or industry.
**Expectations on Salary****
**Earnings of dentists in France** vary greatly depending on experience, location, employment arrangement, working hours, specialization and whether the dentist is employed or self-employed.
**Do Foreign Students Have the Right to Work in France?****

Graduating doesn’t mean you automatically get unlimited **work rights**. International graduates also need to satisfy the **professional registration requirements for dentistry** and the **immigration conditions** that apply to their circumstances.

sections.title: 10. Documents Required to Study Dentistry in France**

items: The **documents required to study dentistry in France** will differ depending on the university and the application process. Typical documents include:
* - **Valid passport**.
* - Certificates and Marksheets of Class 10 and Class 12, if applicable.
* - **Academic certificates and transcripts** of any previous higher education.
* - **Certificate of proficiency in the French language**, if required.
* - **Statement of purpose/motivation letter** (if required).
* - **Resume** (if relevant).
* - **Application forms and documentation**.
* - **Certified translations** of the documents not accepted in the original language.
* - Proof of **payment of application fee**, if applicable.
* - **Letter of admission or acceptance**.
* - Proof of **funds** for the purpose of the visa.
* - Accommodation details if requested.
* - Required documents for the **student visa application**.
